caption:
Perplexity Brain is not another preferences blob. It remembers what the Computer agent did, then synthesizes that work into a context graph on a schedule (including overnight runs).

That shift matters for security. User taste memory optimizes engagement. Work memory optimizes performance, but it also persists sessions, connector results, corrections, and sources unless you govern it.

Perplexity says early first-party runs on repeated tasks showed about 25 percent higher answer correctness, 16 percent higher recall, and 13 percent lower cost when historical context mattered. Treat those numbers as a vendor signal until your team replays the same workflows locally.

Defender move: define retention and deletion for work graphs, audit provenance links after user corrections, and block agents from auto-loading memory that touched sensitive connectors without a human diff.

narration.text: Perplexity Brain does not optimize your tastes. It remembers what the agent did and tries to do the job better next time.
It builds a traceable context graph, then synthesizes sessions and corrections on a schedule, including overnight.
That is performance upside and a new custody problem if connector output and corrections pile up without policy.
Set retention, export, and review provenance before production data touches the graph again.
